mods.name: Obsidian API
mods.summary: A library other mods build on. It does nothing by itself.
mods.description:
A library for [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mods on HELLDIVERS (2015). It gives other mods the game data by name, checked changes that can be undone, and ready actions. It does nothing by itself.

## How to use

Obsidian API comes with Obsidian, in the Obsidian Kit. Mods that need it switch it on with them.

To build on it, list it in the `obsidian.json` of the mod:

```json
"requires": ["obsidian.api"]
```

Then ask for it in the script:

```lua
local api = obsidian.import("obsidian.api")

obsidian.keybind("panic", function()
  api.player.heal()
  api.enemies.kill_near(20)
end)
```

Actions answer `true`, or `false` and a short reason such as `"host_only"`. A client mod can require the API and stay a client mod: it can read game data and use the interface, sound and event calls, and anything that changes the shared game answers `false, "needs_session"`.

[REFERENCE.md](REFERENCE.md) has every call, with guides and recipes. A copy sits in the folder of the API in the Obsidian Kit, where an AI tool working on a mod can read it.

## Known issues

- Tested solo and offline, not yet with a second player.

option_list.label: Open the menu with a controller
option_list.description: The buttons that open and close the F6 menu from a controller, pressed together. In the menu, the D-pad or the left stick moves, A selects, B goes back, Y resets a row, and LB and RB switch pages.

versions.notes:
- Fixed: `catalog.stratagem` and the item lists checked every item against the paid packs on each call, which cost several milliseconds a frame for a mod that looks stratagems up every frame. The answers are now kept for 5 seconds, and `catalog.stratagem` looks up one name.
- Changed: wider gaps between the columns of the Script Profiler panel.

- New: Script Profiler, a page of the F6 window. A panel in the top left corner, on a 20% black background, lists every running mod with the time the scripts of the mod take each frame and the FPS that costs; a name too long for the column scrolls. The page sets where it shows (hidden, pause menu only, always), the detail (basic, or with the slowest frame, calls a frame and the total), how many mods it lists, the corner and the text size. Needs a loader with `obsidian.profiler`.
- New: while the Script Profiler is not hidden, a report goes to the log of Obsidian API every 10 seconds: the frame time, and for each mod the time, slowest frame, calls and the hooks and parts the time goes to. The parts of the frame of Obsidian API are measured one by one.
- Changed: the folder of Obsidian API in the F6 window comes after the folders of the mods.

- Fixed: a client mod listening through `api.events` hears events in any lobby, also while a session or hybrid mod has the API wait for a cleared lobby. Listeners of session mods still wait.
- Changed: with a session or hybrid mod requiring the API, Mod Settings in the pause menu, screenshots, the map, music and `api.lobby` keep working in a lobby that isn't cleared; effects, edits, bots and the rest of what changes the shared game still wait for a cleared lobby.

- New: `api.world.pickups` lists the weapons, backpacks and ammo lying on the ground and `api.world.remove_pickup` deletes one for every machine through the game's own destruction. The owner removes at once, the host asks the owner, any other client is refused.
- New: effects `aim_move_speed` and `reload_move_speed` set how fast the player moves while aiming or reloading, and let a weapon that holds the player in place be walked with.
- Fixed: a bot holds the aim for a moment before the first shot of a weapon, longer and until the barrel is level with a heavy weapon, so a recoilless rifle no longer fires at the ground.
- Fixed: `bot:deliver` drops the thing once the game counts the drop-off as near and the bot can get no closer, and walks to a spot beside a collection point it cannot enter.
- Fixed: a game function's nil results survive the API's hooks, so a hooked function that answers nil still answers nil.
- Fixed: with the Third Person Camera mod, a bot behind the camera gets the off-screen arrow on the side where it stands, not a name mirrored onto the screen.
- Fixed: with the Third Person Camera mod, bots no longer pass as a player at a pad, so the camera stays on the player and bots keep their own aim and buttons.
- Fixed: with the Third Person Camera mod, `api.world.cursor` answers the point under the crosshair.
- Changed: manual stratagem unlocks stay in `obsidian.storage` on a loader without `obsidian.save_data`.
- Changed: manual unlocks of custom stratagems (`api.stratagems.unlock`) go with the save through `obsidian.save_data`. Unlocks kept before this move to the Official save only.

- New: bare bots show the game's off-screen arrow, on every machine; the HUD card stays away.
- New: `bot:add_ammo` adds magazines or rounds through the game's own command.
- New: `api.brain` `engages` and `burst`; a "threat" fight leaves far enemies that haven't noticed the squad alone, holds fire on anything behind cover and fires automatic rifles in short bursts.
- Changed: navigating bots keep a body-width off pit rims, stand rather than walk on with no route, look further ahead with speed, are checked last of every walk source, and return to the last solid spot when knocked over an edge.
- Changed: a bot whose follow spot is across a pit or a long way round takes a spot on the near side of the leader.
- New: `api.nav` finds walking routes around walls, pits, lava, deep water and danger zones with rays over a grid: `path`, `walkable`, `walk_clear`, `zones`, `available`, `search_grid`.
- New: `api.brain`, the pure decisions bots use: weapon choice by threat, target commitment, aim window, blast and line-of-fire checks, formation spots, sprinting, grenades.
- New: `bot:navigate` routes and guards a bot's walking; `bot:movement` adds smooth turning, spacing, varied spots, strafing and sprinting to catch up; `bot:auto_grenades` throws grenades by rule.
- New: `fight` weapon "threat" saves support and heavy weapons for what deserves them, commits to one target, and never fires a blast that would catch a friend.
- New: `api.gear.blast` gives the blast radius of what a weapon fires; `api.enemies.tentacles` lists the Impaler's tentacles, and they count in `api.bots.hazards` and `avoid_shots`'s close attacks.
- Changed: bare bots start out of the camera's framing and the screen leash, and can spawn off the screen.
- New: guest bots can be added from any machine, with looks, pickups and melee dodging, and a mod can tell which peers have left.
- New: a default bot loadout, and `fight` stays within the range of the weapon, with a "best" weapon choice.
- New: `api.stratagems.define` places a stratagem by type or `after` another, and takes descriptions of up to 600 characters.
- New: `api.world.projectile` fires the game's homing missiles, with an optional target to chase from launch.
- Changed: `api.edits` keeps settings variants that mods add.

- New: `api.stratagems.hide(name)` takes a game stratagem out of the Arsenal, the Loadout screen, the default and saved loadouts and the mission inventory; `unhide` and `is_hidden` go with it.
- New: `api.stratagems.carry(name)` gives every player a stratagem as an extra entry in missions, beyond the 8 loadout slots, and other players' HUDs show it; `uncarry` and `is_carried` go with it.
- New: `api.stratagems.share_cooldown(name)` puts the whole squad on one cooldown for a stratagem; `unshare_cooldown` and `is_shared` go with it.
- Changed: when several stratagems share an arrow code, the one the player holds and can use wins.
- Changed: the Loadout screen filters and orders the lists the game reads, so a custom stratagem sits beside the base there too.
- Changed: the label of the F6 key says "Open in-game menu" in French, Spanish, Portuguese and Chinese too, as in English since 1.36.2.

- New: `bot:operate(unit, opts, on_done)` works a terminal to the end: objective terminals, the extraction beacon and hidden objects. Arrows go in one frame each, checked before the next, and presses come at a set rate. `bot:operating()` and `bot:cancel_operate()` go with it.
- New: `bot:deliver(unit, pos, opts, on_done)` carries a thing an objective asks for to the drop-off and puts it down there. `bot:delivering()` goes with it.
- New: `api.mission.drop_offs(thing)` lists where carried things count as delivered.
- New: `bot:load(unit, opts, on_done)` loads a teammate's recoilless rifle or missile launcher from the bot's backpack.
- New: `bot:take_ammo(unit, opts, on_done)` takes ammo from a teammate's ammo backpack, or from the bot's own.
- New: `api.bots.dead()` lists the players the next reinforcement brings back, and `bot:reinforce(pos, on_done)` calls it.
- New: `api.mission.extraction()` reads the beacon and the shuttle, `api.mission.aboard(unit)` says who got in, and `bot:board(opts, on_done)` walks a bot into the shuttle. A bare bot aboard leaves the level.
- New: `bot:detonate()` sets off the satchel charges the bot threw, and `bot:charges_out()` counts them.
- New: `api.bots.hazards(pos, radius, kinds)` lists mines, burning areas and armed hellbombs near a point.
- New: `api.mission.areas()` lists the hold and fortify areas with their radius and progress.
- New: `bot:camera(false)`, or `api.bots.add({ free_camera = true })`, takes a player bot out of the camera's framing and the screen's edge, so it walks anywhere on the map. `bot:in_camera()` goes with it.
- New: `use_weapon` takes `move`, to keep walking on the bot's orders while it fires, and `rest`, seconds the weapon stays put away afterwards. `bot:resting(slot)` says how long.
- New: `bot:use` takes `force`, to have the game use the thing with no wait for the game to offer it.
- Changed: a bot sent to use something stops a little short when the thing's own body keeps it from getting closer, as with the extraction beacon.

- Changed: a fighting bot fires only once it faces the target and has held on it a moment, so a shot doesn't leave on the way round, where a teammate may stand.
- Changed: in a mech, the bot lines up the gun on the mech's arm with the target, not the mech's middle.
- Changed: a driving bot eases off near the point it drives to and stops within 4 meters of it, or when the point ends up close behind, instead of circling it.
- Changed: a dead body in the way no longer stops a bot's shot.
- Changed: `bot:use` takes out the primary when the game offers the bot a reload of the bot's own first (an empty recoilless with the recoilless backpack), so the thing it was sent to use comes through.
- Changed: a new `fight` order looks for a target at once.
- Changed: `bot:use_weapon` reloads an empty launcher that the bot's backpack reloads before taking back the weapon from before, so the reload plays and the launcher comes out loaded next time.
- Fixed: with `freeze` on, a killed enemy falls and despawns while the rest stay frozen.
- Fixed: effects no longer log an error each time they're switched on outside a mission.

- New: `bot:hurts(target, slot)` and `api.gear.hurts(weapon, target)` answer the damage one hit does to a target after armor: square, glancing and on the weak spot, launchers included. An enemy the rifle gets 0 against is one for the anti-tank weapon.
- New: `api.enemies.charging(unit)` reads an enemy about to shoot (the Hunter's beam, the Cyborg IFV's laser sight, the Hulk's wind-up): when it fires and where the aim line runs.
- New: `bot:avoid_shots(true)` gets the bot out of that line, with a dive just before the shot. `bot:avoiding()` goes with it.
- New: `fight`'s `secondary` takes `only` and `every`.
- New: `bot:position()` answers where the bot stands.
- New: `bot:mech_friendly_fire(false)` keeps the mech a bot pilots from hurting Helldivers. Enemies still take the hits.
- Changed: a bot in an exosuit fires the rockets one each second, and only while it faces the target. Before, it emptied the rack at once.
- Changed: `bot:throw()` does nothing in a vehicle seat, where the button fires the vehicle's second weapon.
- Fixed: bots stand still while session mods are off. Before, each one kept the last buttons and sticks it was given, and the game went on reading those every frame.

mods.name: Obsidian Patches
mods.summary: Small fixes and conveniences for the game.
mods.description:
Small fixes for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

Obsidian Patches removes the black bars on wide screens, skips the intro, the login screen and the planet scans, speeds up the mission end, pauses the game in solo missions, and fixes the recoil and sprint animations.

## How to use

Obsidian Patches comes with Obsidian, in the Obsidian Kit, switched on. Each fix is an option in Obsidian and takes effect at the next launch. Four of them can also be changed in game, under **Mods** in the pause menu, and apply at once.

option_list.label: Widescreen fixes
option_list.description: No black bars on screens wider than 16:9, and the objective list, dialogue boxes and galaxy map panels at the real edges of the screen.

option_list.label: Expedite mission end
option_list.description: Faster gives each results screen about a second. Instant skips to the last one. Rewards are saved either way.

option_list.label: Skip intro
option_list.description: No logos or intro video at launch.

option_list.label: Skip login screen
option_list.description: Starts on the ship, still online, with keyboard and mouse as the player 1 controls.

option_list.label: Skip war briefs
option_list.description: Hides the war briefs at login and on the galaxy map, including the updates shown as the war moves. The end of a war still plays.

option_list.label: Skip planet scanning
option_list.description: No planet discovery animation after a liberation or a new sector.

option_list.label: Dynamic solo pause
option_list.description: With a single player in the mission, the pause menu freezes the game, even in a public or friends-only lobby. The game resumes as soon as someone joins.

option_list.label: Aim cursor always visible
option_list.description: On PC, the cursor keeps the aiming look at all times, instead of dimming between shots.

option_list.label: Toggle minimap
option_list.description: The map key opens the minimap and keeps it open until pressed again, instead of only while held.

option_list.label: Weapon recoil animation fix
option_list.description: Every weapon taken in hand plays the matching recoil animation, whatever was in hand before.

option_list.label: Sprint pose fix
option_list.description: Sprinting right after getting up from a dive shows the normal running pose, instead of an upper body stuck until the sprint starts over.

versions.notes:
- Changed: **Skip war briefs** also hides the briefs the open galaxy map plays when the war moves, such as a sector changing hands or a defend event ending. The end of a war still plays, at login too.
- Changed: **Weapon recoil animation fix** works after any weapon change, for every Helldiver in the session. A heavy support weapon, a revolver or plasma pistol shot, or a switch while aiming used to leave the next weapon with the recoil of another weapon, or none.
- Removed: **Dynamic input switch**. Keyboard, mouse and gamepad together clashed in menus such as the galaxy map.

- Changed: with **Dynamic input switch** on, logging in reaches the ship again. The join a gamepad's press asks for waited for the hold, and so did the request that adds the first player when a session starts, which left the ship without a Helldiver and returned to the main menu. Only the press waits now.

- Changed: **Widescreen fixes** also puts the mission's objective list in the top right corner of the screen and dialogue boxes (the ship's characters, briefings) at the left edge, instead of inside the 16:9 middle.
- Changed: **Widescreen fixes** also moves the galaxy map's planet panel, the planet's reward and mission panels to the screen's edges, and stretches the galaxy map's scanline overlay across the whole screen.

- Changed: going online works again. 1.9.0 sent some of the game's network messages with one value too many, which ended the session after login and returned to the main menu, with Dynamic input switch on or off.

- New: **Dynamic input switch**, off by default. With a keyboard and a gamepad connected, both control the first Helldiver and the button prompts follow the last one used; the gamepad joins as a second Helldiver only when its join button is held for 1.5 seconds, and the prompt reads HOLD instead of PRESS.
- Changed: a new image beside the mod in Obsidian's mod list.
- Changed: Sprint pose fix now frees the upper body when a sprint starts straight from standing, which is how a sprint starts after getting up from a dive, and after firing or a weapon switch too.

- Changed: Weapon recoil after stratagems is now Weapon recoil animation fix, and also brings the recoil animation back after picking up a weapon from the ground.
- Changed: Sprint pose after a dive is now Sprint pose fix.
- Changed: Widescreen fixes and Expedite mission end come first in the option list.

- Changed: the mod is now Obsidian Patches, in Obsidian and in the pause menu, where the page title reads the name in full.
- New: Weapon recoil after stratagems brings back the recoil animation of the weapon in hand when a stratagem throw leaves it out. On by default.
- New: Sprint pose after a dive keeps the running pose normal when sprinting right after getting up from a dive. On by default.
- Changed: the French, Spanish and Portuguese pause menu rows show accented letters correctly.

mods.name: Obsidian Trainer
mods.summary: An in-game menu that changes the character, gear, enemies and missions.
mods.description:
An in-game menu for HELLDIVERS (2015) that changes the character, weapons, stratagems, enemies, missions and game data, for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

Missions add nothing to the save while the Trainer is on, and it stays out of the Galactic War. It offers only the base game and owned DLC.

## How to use

1. Switch on Obsidian Trainer in the Mods tab. [Obsidian API](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianAPI) turns on with it.
2. Deploy, then start the game.
3. Press **F6** to open the menu. The key can be changed in the Keys tab of Obsidian API.

The Obsidian Trainer page in the Wiki of Obsidian lists every key and page.

option_list.label: Keep saved edits
option_list.description: Applies the kept edits each time the game starts. The multiplayer check can't see them, so they belong in lobbies where everyone agreed to them.

versions.notes:
- New: Move speed while aiming and Move speed while reloading on the Player page, which let weapons that hold the player in place be walked with.
- Fixed: on a loader without `obsidian.save_data` the Mission page rows stay open, as before saves came in.
- Fixed: with the Third Person Camera mod, the rows that act at the cursor take the point under the crosshair. Needs Obsidian API 1.48.0.
- Changed: the Mission page rows that award progression (spawn and collect samples) need a Sandbox save. On an Official save they stay locked and point to the Saves tab.

- New: each bot's page has **Objectives**: work the terminal at the cursor (codes and presses to the end), stop working it, deliver the nearest thing to carry, reinforce at the cursor, board the shuttle, load my launcher, take ammo from my backpack or from the bot's own, and set off satchel charges.
- New: **In the camera** for each bot. Off, the camera no longer frames the bot and it can walk anywhere on the map.
- New: **Support weapon at the cursor, on the move** for each bot: the bot keeps walking while it fires, then puts the weapon away for 10 seconds.
- New: **Use the thing at the cursor, forced** for each bot.
- These rows show with the next Obsidian API.

- Changed: with **Each weapon for what it can hurt**, the bot fires the support weapon until the target dies or the weapon is spent, and looks again a second later: a launcher with several rockets, such as the Commando, fires them all.
- Changed: an order given on the **Bots** page stops a support weapon shot the bot started by itself, and holds those back for 8 seconds. A shot that came to nothing waits 5 seconds before the next.
- Fixed: messages on how a bot's order ended showed "bot_enter_failed" in place of the text.

- Changed: on the **Bots** page, **Fight** is a choice for each bot: **Off**, **Nearest enemy**, **Each weapon for what it can hurt** (the primary for what it gets through the armor of, the support weapon for the rest), **In a vehicle: both weapons**, and **In a mech: gun, then rockets**. All of this release's rows show in full with Obsidian API 1.38.0.
- New: each bot's page has **Weapons** (take out a weapon, the support weapon at the enemy at the cursor, the damage each weapon does to that enemy, refill the backpack), **Vehicles** (get in, take the driver's seat, get out, ride along, a mech that spares Helldivers) and **Using things** (the thing at the cursor or the nearest one, put it down, voice lines, a jump pack jump to the cursor).
- New: **Get out of enemy shots** for each bot and for every bot: the bot walks out of a Hunter's, a Cyborg IFV's or a Hulk's aim before the shot.
- New: on the **Bots** page, **Fight with each weapon for what it can hurt** and **Mechs spare Helldivers** for every bot.
- New: on the **Enemies** page, **Tell me when an enemy aims** and **Armor of the enemy**, with what each of your weapons does to it.
- Changed: a bot that can't follow an order says why in words about the bot: busy, in a seat, a seat someone else took.
- Changed: on the **Bots** page, **Help up the nearest** and **Heal the most hurt** say when another bot is already on the way to everyone who needs it. Needs Obsidian API 1.34.0.

- New: on the **Bots** page, **Help up the nearest**, **Heal the most hurt** and **Heal me** for every bot or one, and **Help each other** and **Stop helping each other** for every bot. Healing uses the REP-80 in the bot's slots. Needs Obsidian API 1.33.0.
- New: each bot's page has **Get up when downed** (on by default), **Help others up**, **Heal others** and **Stop helping**.

- Changed: **Practice mission** is now **Custom mission**, which drops into a real mission. XP, samples and unlocks count. Before, it started a training mission that paid no XP. The campaign stays as it was: no planet progress, and no Galactic War or leaderboard report.

- Changed: **Field of view**, **Camera distance** and **Camera angle** reset to the game's own values for the current screen, on the ship as in missions. They reset to a mission's values before, which left the ship's camera wrong.
- Changed: a new image beside the mod in Obsidian's mod list.

- New: Enter a stratagem on each bot's page: the bot holds the stratagem key, enters the code of a stratagem it carries and throws the flare at the cursor. Stop entering ends it.
- New: Enter a stratagem under Every bot: each bot carrying the chosen stratagem enters it.
- New: the mod's image, shown beside it in Obsidian's mod list.

mods.name: Better HUD
mods.summary: Adds round counts, health bars and damage numbers to the HUD.
mods.description:
More information on the HUD of HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

Better HUD counts the rounds left in the magazine and the grenades on each player card, puts health and stamina bars under the player cards and health bars over enemies, and shows damage numbers where hits land. A reload circle and an ammo circle sit beside the Helldiver. Enemy bars show burns, poison and stuns, and wait at the edge of the screen while the enemy is out of view.

## How to use

Every part can be switched on or off in the options of Better HUD in Obsidian, or in game under **Mods → Better HUD** in the pause menu. A change in one place shows in the other.

## Known issues

- Players on other computers get no stamina bar: the game keeps stamina on each player's computer and never sends it.
- Lasers and arc weapons get no round counter, since they heat or charge up instead. The ammo circle shows their heat or charge.

Mod authors can add meters, flashes and status icons to the HUD through Better HUD: see [docs/api.md](docs/api.md).

option_list.label: Ammo counter
option_list.description: Rounds left in the magazine, over the magazine count, for weapons that fire rounds. Hidden while calling a stratagem.

option_list.label: Grenade counter
option_list.description: Replaces the lower grenade icon on each player card with the number of grenades, such as x3, so counts above two show too.

option_list.label: Player health bars
option_list.description: A red bar under each player card, with a white chunk fading where health was lost and a yellow bar over it while a shield holds. After 10 seconds at full health the bar fades to grey and half opacity.

option_list.label: Health numbers
option_list.description: Current and maximum health at the right of each player bar.

option_list.label: Stamina bar
option_list.description: A thin white bar under the health bar of each player on this computer, emptying while sprinting and filling back up after. After 10 seconds full the bar fades to grey and half opacity. Players on other computers get none, as the game does not send stamina over the network.

option_list.label: Enemy health bars
option_list.description: A bar over every enemy the player hits and every heavy that any player hurts. The bar of an enemy out of view waits at the edge of the screen. In the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person, that bar hides until the enemy is in view.

option_list.label: Reload circle
option_list.description: A ring to the left of each local Helldiver that fills while the weapon in hand reloads.

option_list.label: Ammo circle
option_list.description: A yellow ring beside each local Helldiver with the share of the magazine left, fading to red from 30% to empty. Lasers fill the ring with heat, pulsing between yellow and red from half heat, faster as it heats. Arc weapons fill it in blue with the charge, dim until the charge can fire. Empty or overheated, the ring shakes and flashes red, with the reload button inside. Shows from a shot, hides after a reload, and fades out 8 seconds after the last shot.

option_list.label: Hide on-player health bar
option_list.description: Takes away the game's own red bar over each Helldiver.

option_list.label: Hide on-player recovery bar
option_list.description: Takes away the game's own bar over a downed Helldiver getting back up.

option_list.label: Damage numbers
option_list.description: The damage dealt, where it lands: on enemies the player hits, on players losing health, or both.

option_list.label: Damage numbers mode
option_list.description: Stacked shows a number for each hit, rising out of the way at once. Accumulated adds every hit on one target into one number that stays in place and fades out, and a new one starts only once it is gone.

option_list.label: Damage numbers position
option_list.description: Above health bar needs Enemy health bars, and uses the entity spot where no bar shows. At damage instance uses the spot each hit landed.

versions.notes: - Changed the reload and ammo circles in the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person to half again as big, closer to the middle of the screen, and on the side away from the Helldiver.

- Added the stamina bar option, on by default: a thin white bar under the health bar of each player on this computer, emptying while sprinting and filling back up after. Players on other computers get none, as the game does not send stamina over the network.
- Changed the shield on the player health bars to cover the red over the full height of the bar, in place of the top half.
- Changed the player health bars to a fifth taller, keeping the bottom edge in place, with the health numbers a fifth bigger to match.
- Changed the reload and ammo circles in the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person to a fixed spot half way up the screen, out past the Helldiver on the side away from the camera shoulder. When the camera swaps shoulders, the spot eases across.
- Changed the enemy health bars in the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person to sit a little lower over each enemy.
- Changed the damage numbers on players in the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person to start above the name card over the head.
- Changed the enemy health bars in the shoulder view of Integrated Third Person to hide the bar of an enemy out of view until the enemy is looked at, as with Third Person Camera, in place of holding the bar at the edge of the screen.
- Changed the icon other mods can place on an enemy health bar to half again as big, so the mark reads at a glance.

- Added `elite_mark` for other mods: the health bar of a marked enemy shows from the start and stays while the enemy lives, with the icon the mod gives in the middle of the bar, white with the soft outline of the status icons.
- Fixed: With Third Person Camera on, the health bar of an enemy out of view no longer waits at the edge of the screen. It is hidden until the enemy is looked at.

- Changed the player health bars to about a third thinner, keeping the bottom edge in place.
- Added a fade to the player health bars: after 10 seconds at full health a bar turns grey at 50% opacity, and returns when health is lost or a shield drops below full.
- Changed the health numbers on the player bars to a smaller size to fit.
- Changed the shadow of damage numbers to half the distance from the number.
- Changed the shadow around the status icons over enemy health bars to less than half as dark.
- Fixed `status_effect` for other mods, which stopped with an error when given the seconds as text.
- Fixed a possible crash when the health bar of an enemy that was already gone looked up the enemy kind.

- Fixed the grenade counter and the grenade charge meter, which never showed: the size of the grenade icon was read in a way the game does not support.

mods.name: Photo Mode
mods.summary: Stops the game and frees the camera for pictures.
mods.description:
A photo mode for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

Photo Mode stops the mission, clears the HUD and hands over the camera. A panel of controls sets the lens, depth of field, filters, fog, the time of day and the sun, places up to eight lights, and poses the Helldiver. Pictures are saved to `Pictures\Helldivers`.

## How to use

Press **F7**, or pick **PHOTO MODE** in the pause menu, during a mission or on the ship. Esc or F7 leaves, and everything goes back as it was.

| Key | What it does |
|---|---|
| W A S D, Q E | Move the camera |
| Right mouse button | Look around |
| Mouse wheel | Field of view, distance or zoom |
| Shift, Alt | Faster, slower |
| Left mouse button, twice | Focus on the point under the cursor |
| P | Take a picture |
| H | Hide or show the panel |

P, H and F7 can be changed in the Keys tab of Photo Mode in Obsidian.

## Known issues

- With other players in the lobby the game keeps running, as pausing one game would split it from the others.
- In exclusive fullscreen, pictures can come out black. Borderless or windowed mode works.
- Photo Mode does not open while Third Person Camera is installed.

option_list.description: Clears the part of the picture past the level, where the game leaves smears of old frames, and adds the skies of the Sky row. Takes effect at the next launch.

mods.name: Enhanced Visuals
mods.summary: Enhances graphics and adds extra visual effects.
mods.description:
Better graphics and extra visual effects for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

The mod turns on the ambient occlusion pass that the game ships but never runs, adds sharpening and an ambient light effect, raises the resolution and distance of sun shadows, softens shadow edges, keeps detailed models farther from the camera, and can draw the scene above the screen resolution.

## How to use

**F9** switches between Enhanced Visuals and the plain game, to compare. The key can be changed in Obsidian.

For the game textures at twice the size, see [Upscaled Textures](https://github.com/Alomare/HD1-UpscaledTextures), a separate mod that works with or without this one.

## Known issues

- Third Person Camera also uses F9: with both mods on, change one of the keys. Put Enhanced Visuals after Third Person Camera in the load order, or the shadow and render scale options do nothing.
- A shadow resolution of 8192 takes 256 MB of video memory.

option_list.label: Screen dust
option_list.description: The layer of dust that drifts across the picture on most planets.

option_list.label: Sharpening
option_list.description: Restores the fine detail that anti-aliasing softens, with less at strong edges so they don't ring. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Ambient light
option_list.description: Deepens the dark tones and spreads a soft glow around lit areas, in place of the game's bloom. The HUD keeps the game's colors. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Desert ambient light
option_list.description: Ambient light in daytime missions on desert planets. Off by default, as the bright sand makes the picture too bright with it. Applies at once.

option_list.label: Ambient occlusion
option_list.description: Darkens the light where surfaces meet, such as at the foot of walls and under crates and rocks.

option_list.label: Ambient occlusion affects
option_list.description: Ambient light darkens only the light from the sky, so the effect shows mostly in shade. All daylight darkens sunlight too.

option_list.label: Shadow resolution
option_list.description: The size of the sun's shadow map; larger gives sharper shadows. 8192 uses 256 MB of video memory. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Shadow distance
option_list.description: How far from the camera the sun casts shadows. The game stops at about 20 m, which can leave the top of the screen without shadows when zoomed out. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Shadow edges
option_list.description: Softens the hard, stepped edges of sun shadows. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Render scale
option_list.description: Draws the scene above the screen's resolution and scales it down, for cleaner edges. 2x costs about four times the pixel work. Takes effect at the next launch.

option_list.label: Model detail distance
option_list.description: How far from the camera models keep their most detailed version.

versions.notes:
- New: Desert ambient light, off by default: in daytime missions on desert planets, Ambient light stays off, as the bright sand made the picture too bright. Turning the option on keeps the effect there. It applies at once, also from the pause menu.
- Changed: Shadow distance now covers every time of day and every area lighting of the planets. Before, only one lighting set per planet got the longer distance, so most missions kept the game distance whatever the option said.
- Changed: Enhanced Visuals loads after Integrated Third Person, which replaces the render config too.
- New: Enhanced Textures, an optional download beside this release: game textures at twice the size, upscaled by an AI model. Import the zip into Obsidian like any other mod.

- Changed: Render scale no longer draws glass, such as the shield on the ship, over the objects behind it.
- New: A thumbnail for Obsidian.

- New: Ambient light, in the manner of the Ambient Light shader for ReShade: deeper dark tones and a wide, soft glow around lit areas, Subtle or Strong.
- New: Ambient occlusion, a pass the game ships but never runs, now on with a new shader: darker light where surfaces meet, Subtle or Strong, on ambient light or on all daylight.
- New: Sharpening after anti-aliasing, Normal or Strong.
- New: Shadow resolution: the sun shadow map at 4096 or 8192, past the 2048 of the Graphics menu.
- New: Shadow distance: sun shadows reach 35 m or 60 m from the camera instead of about 20 m.
- New: Shadow edges: Soft and Softer sun shadow edges, at every shadow resolution.
- New: Render scale: the scene at 1.5 or 2 times the screen resolution, scaled down before the HUD.
- New: Model detail distance: models keep the most detailed version two or four times farther from the camera.
- New: Screen dust: the dust that drifts across the picture on most planets is off by default, with an option to bring it back.
- New: F9 switches between Enhanced Visuals and the original look of the game, to compare.

mods.name: Unleashed Camera
mods.summary: Third person and first person cameras that keep other mods working.
mods.description:
Third person and first person cameras for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager. Formerly Integrated Third Person: remove that mod when installing this one. Based on [Third Person Camera (HD2 Style)](https://github.com/yukiorsrs/third-person-camera-helldivers) by **yukiorsrs**, rebuilt with the permission of the author so that other mods keep working beside it.

The camera follows the Helldiver over the shoulder on foot, in vehicles and on the ship, or from the eyes of the Helldiver in first person. Shots, grenades and stratagems go where the crosshair points. The view reaches farther, the sky over the level is filled in, a ring around the crosshair warns of enemies close by, and a bar shows where hits come from.

Third Person Camera replaces 28 game scripts, so mods that change the same parts of the game stop working with it. Unleashed Camera replaces no script: every change is a hook through Obsidian.

## How to use

**F8** cycles the camera: the top-down camera of the game, third person, and first person. **H** swaps the shoulder. Both keys can be changed in Obsidian.

## Playing with others

The camera and everything on screen work in any lobby. Four session features change the game for the whole lobby: Max weapon range, Far enemy detection, Free movement and Increased throw range. They run only when every player runs Obsidian with the same mods, and switch off when anyone else joins. With all four off, the mod counts as a client mod.

## Known issues

- Players on one computer share a screen, so the camera goes back to top-down while a second local player is in, and comes back after.
- The mod stays off while Third Person Camera is installed.
- First person is new: vehicles keep the third-person camera.

Mod authors can read the camera state through `obsidian.import("alomare.unleashedcamera")`: `active()`, `mode()`, `crosshair()` and `shoulder()`.

mods.name: Custom Crosshair
mods.summary: Replaces the aim cursor with a custom crosshair and adds a hitmarker.
mods.description:
A crosshair mod for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager.

Custom Crosshair replaces the aim cursor with a crosshair built from shapes, with one look between shots and another while aiming. Shape, size, gap, color, outline and shadow are all settings. A hitmarker flashes around the crosshair when a shot from this player hurts or kills an enemy.

## How to use

The settings are in the Options tab of Custom Crosshair in Obsidian, with a live preview. A change applies at the next launch of the game.

With Unleashed Camera, the crosshair goes where shots land. Turn off **Third person crosshair** to keep the crosshair of the game there instead, or **First person crosshair** for no crosshair in first person.

## Known issues

- On a controller the game shows no cursor in the top-down view, so no crosshair shows there.
- A shot that armor stops does not count as a hit.

option_list.label: Custom crosshair
option_list.description: Draws the crosshair set here in place of the game cursor, in missions and on the ship. The menu cursor stays as it is.

option_list.label: Third person crosshair
option_list.description: With Unleashed Camera, draws this crosshair where shots go, in place of the one from that mod. The game has no cursor in third person, so a state set to Game cursor uses the default look there.

option_list.description: While a laser weapon fires, the crosshair spins up to one turn a second within 0.05 seconds, and winds down over half a second once firing stops.

option_list.label: Idle shape
option_list.description: Game cursor keeps the cursor of the game; None shows no crosshair at all.

option_list.label: Idle scale

option_list.description: Space between the center and the lines. Also sets how wide circles, brackets and the chevron sit.

option_list.description: 1 is solid. The outline and the shadow fade with the lines.

option_list.description: A border around every line, so the crosshair stands out on light and dark ground.

option_list.description: Size of the whole crosshair, outline and shadow included. At 1 the pixel sizes below are drawn as set.

option_list.label: Aiming gap (px)
option_list.description: Space between the center and the lines. Also sets how wide circles, brackets and the chevron sit.

option_list.label: Aiming length (px)
option_list.description: Length of each line. Circles, brackets and the chevron grow with it.

option_list.label: Aiming gap scales with spread
option_list.description: Opens the aiming gap by up to 12 pixels as the spread of the weapon in hand grows while firing, and closes it as the spread settles.

option_list.label: Aiming thickness (px)
option_list.description: Width of the lines. The dot is twice as wide.

option_list.label: Aiming opacity
option_list.description: 1 is solid. The outline and the shadow fade with the lines.

option_list.label: Aiming outline
option_list.description: A border around every line, so the crosshair stands out on light and dark ground.

option_list.label: Aiming shadow
option_list.description: A copy behind the crosshair, moved down and to the right.

option_list.label: Aiming shadow offset (px)
option_list.description: Distance down and to the right.

option_list.label: Aiming shadow size
option_list.description: Scales the shadow around the center of the crosshair. Below 1 the shadow shrinks inside the lines; above 1 it reaches past them.

option_list.label: Aiming shadow spread (px)
option_list.description: Widens the shadow by this many pixels on every side, on top of the outline width.

option_list.label: Aiming shadow blur (px)
option_list.description: Softens the shadow edge with fainter copies up to this many pixels out. 0 keeps a sharp edge.

option_list.label: Hitmarker
option_list.description: Shows four short diagonal lines around the crosshair on a hit, at full strength first, then fading out over the time set below.

option_list.label: Show on hits
option_list.description: Every hit that costs an enemy health shows the mark in the hit color.

option_list.label: Show on kills
option_list.description: A kill shows the mark in the kill color, over any hit mark still fading.

option_list.label: Hits from
option_list.description: Weapons in hand counts shots from the primary, the sidearm and the support weapon. Rockets, grenades, mines, sentries and stratagems count only with Everything.

option_list.label: Hit opacity
option_list.description: How strong a hit mark shows at first, before the fade. 1 is solid.

option_list.label: Kill opacity
option_list.description: How strong a kill mark shows at first, before the fade. 1 is solid.

option_list.label: Kill mark scale
option_list.description: A kill mark is this many times the size of a hit mark: line length, gap and thickness alike.

option_list.label: Hitmarker size (px)
option_list.description: Length of each line.

option_list.label: Hitmarker gap (px)
option_list.description: Distance from the center of the crosshair to the inner end of each line, along the diagonal.

option_list.label: Hitmarker thickness (px)
option_list.description: Width of the lines.

option_list.label: Hitmarker time (s)
option_list.description: How long a mark takes to fade out. A new hit starts the fade again.

option_list.label: Hitmarker outline
option_list.description: A black border one pixel wide, so the mark stands out on light ground.

versions.notes: - Changed: the options name Unleashed Camera, the new name of Integrated Third Person.

- New: the crosshair fades out while sprinting in Integrated Third Person 0.6.0 and later.
- New: First person crosshair option, for the first person camera of Integrated Third Person. Off leaves first person with no crosshair.
- New: Laser spin option, on by default. While a laser weapon fires, the crosshair spins up to one turn a second, and winds down over about half a second once firing stops, ending upright.
- Changed: new default look: a dot between shots, and a longer cross with a wider gap while aiming, both with a soft shadow. The hitmarker is smaller and thicker by default, and the kill mark a little bigger.
- Fixed: with Aiming gap scales with spread, the gap stayed open after firing until the next shot, instead of closing as the spread recovers.

- New: Idle length and Aiming length set how long each line is, 8 pixels by default. Circles, brackets and the chevron grow with it.
- Changed: new default look. Idle is a faint white circle 3 pixels thick; aiming is a white cross 3 pixels thick with a thin outline and a soft shadow; hit marks are white and kill marks red, with no outline. Settings already saved stay as they are.
- Changed: in third person with Integrated Third Person 0.4.2 or later, the aiming crosshair also shows while fire or a throw is held, as in the top-down view.

- New: Aiming gap scales with spread, on by default. The aiming gap opens by up to 12 pixels as the spread of the weapon in hand grows while firing, and closes as the spread settles.
- Changed: number settings go in steps of 0.01, and every one starts at 0. Shadow blur keeps whole pixels.
- Fixed: the game cursor no longer shows over the crosshair in the top-down view.

- Changed: hit marks are red, as kill marks are, and start at 60% opacity.
- Changed: kill marks are solid and one and a half times the size of hit marks.
- Changed: hitmarker lines are twice as long by default.
- New: Hit opacity, Kill opacity and Kill mark scale options.

- New: hitmarker, four diagonal lines around the crosshair that fade out after a hit or a kill. Options for hits, kills, which weapons count, hit and kill color, size, gap, thickness, fade time and outline, with a live preview. Needs Obsidian API.
- New: shadow size, spread and blur.
- Changed: the idle and aiming crosshairs fade into each other in 0.08 seconds.

- New: replaces the aim cursor of the game with a crosshair built from shapes, with one look between shots and another while aiming, in missions and on the ship.
- New: shapes for each look: cross, cross with dot, dot, circle, circle with dot, circle with cross, T, chevron, brackets, the game cursor or none, with scale, gap, thickness, color, opacity, outline and shadow.
- New: option groups in Obsidian with live previews of the crosshair. The groups and previews need Obsidian 2.0.0.
- New: with Integrated Third Person, the crosshair goes where shots land.

mods.name: Helldivers Arcade
mods.summary: Arcade game modes, starting with a horde survival mode.
mods.description:
Arcade game modes for HELLDIVERS (2015), for the [Obsidian](https://github.com/Alomare/ObsidianLauncher) mod manager. The first mode is Super Earth Survivors.

## Super Earth Survivors

A mode inspired by Vampire Survivors. The squad drops on an open map and holds out against waves that grow stronger over time. A second faction joins at 6 minutes and the third at 12, with elites, bosses and bombardments along the way.

Kills drop research samples. Each level up freezes the fight, refills health and lets every player pick one of three upgrade cards; every third level adds a stratagem. Some upgrades come in pairs that can evolve into a stronger one. The shuttle can be called after 15 minutes, and a summary of the run shows at the end.

## How to use

Open the galaxy map and pick the **ARCADE** tab, beside Proving Grounds. Choose the faction, the difficulty and the biome, then Launch. The next drop plays the same mission again until a campaign mission is picked.

Arcade missions leave the Galactic Campaign as it was.

## Playing with others

Until the host picks an arcade mission, the mod runs as a client mod and anyone can join. An arcade mission needs every player in the lobby to run Helldivers Arcade at the same version.

versions.notes:
- New: a 3 second countdown after the landing, drawn like the hellpod launch countdown. When it ends, the alarm goes on and stays on. Enemies never raise an alarm, and every enemy knows where the squad is and comes for it.
- New: a Fire elite leaves a wide fire where it dies, for 15 seconds.
- Changed: Noxious and Fire elites move faster, by half of the Swift boost.
- Changed: toxic ground from a Noxious elite shows a poison cloud on every machine.
- Changed: Cluster Grenade blasts land closer together (3.5 m instead of 6 m) and follow each other faster (0.15 s instead of 0.3 s).
- Changed: upgrades already held come up less often in the cards (twice as likely as a new one instead of three times).
- Changed: a ground full of samples (300) sets off the sample vacuum early instead of merging the oldest.
- Changed: the Script Profiler of Obsidian API shows the parts of the frame of a run one by one.
- Fixed: a reinforcement that came just as the last player died could leave the defeat summary up for good. The summary now closes as soon as a player is on the way back.

- New: Elite tools on the debug page: base unit, count and distance for spawned elites, a random kind, pausing elite spawns for the run, the next elite now, killing or removing every elite, breaking the Bulwark dome, and a status line.
- Changed: Cluster Grenade, Carpet Bombing, Sweet Liberty and Chain Reaction blasts show the fireball and play the sound of a player grenade, on every machine. Before, they did damage unseen.
- Changed: the first alarm is again the one the enemy raises. The first moments of a run for the host no longer count as taking over from a host that left, which raised the alarm at once.
- Changed: Shock elites only arc while a Helldiver out of the drop pod is within range, so a landing player is no longer hit, and the arcs do half damage to other enemies.
- Changed: the three panels of the Arcade screen span the width of the screen, staying within the middle 16:9 on wider screens.
- Changed: the Mission Preview shows the planet name in the top right corner of the map.
- Changed: the difficulty bar sits inside the difficulty selector, under the name.
- Changed: the upgrade panel of the map spaces the badges more closely, and shows the rerolls and banishes in larger text under the upgrades.
- Changed: the partner icons on an upgrade card are a tenth bigger and centred between the badge and the edge of the card.
- Changed: the icon of an elite is half again as big with Better HUD 1.17.0.

- New: a weapon dropped on the ground vanishes after a minute. Weapons in the crate of a stratagem stay.
- New: on a defeat, the combat music stops and the defeat music of the game plays.
- Changed: the first alarm is the one the enemy raises, with the scream or flare. The Arcade keeps the alarm on from then.
- Changed: the end-of-run summary shows at once instead of 2 seconds after the end.
- Changed: an upgrade card shows the partner icons of an evolution to the right of the badge, a fifth bigger.
- Changed: the dome of a Bulwark elite rides on the elite instead of being placed again as it walks. Anyone walks through it, and shots from outside stop on it.
- Changed: the level and clock in the top bar and the end-of-run summary use the body font instead of the title font.
- Removed: chests.
- Changed: the health bar of an elite shows all the time, with an icon for the kind in the middle of the bar, in place of the colored glow under the elite and the name over it. Needs Better HUD 1.16.0.
- Changed: needs Obsidian API 1.48.0.

- New: **Super Earth Survivors**, the first arcade game mode, picked from the ARCADE tab beside Proving Grounds on the galaxy map, with the starting faction, the difficulty and the map chosen there.
- New: enemies come in waves of 30 seconds with a 20 second break, more and stronger as time goes on. A second faction joins at 6:00 and a third at 12:00, elites come from 3:00, a boss at 10:00 and 20:00 and then every 5 minutes, and red strike bombardments fall near the squad from 7:00.
- New: kills drop research samples, and every level-up offers upgrade cards (common, rare, legendary, perk and evolution) and, every few levels, stratagems, with rerolls and banishes.
- New: upgrades for weapons, movement, health and armor, grenades, melee and stratagems, and evolutions that join two upgrades into one with a new effect.
- New: chests from elites, bosses and rare kills, with upgrades for every player in the squad.
- New: the shuttle can be called after 15 minutes, and a run ends with a summary: the result, the time survived, the level, the factions, the bosses and the damage of each player by source.
- New: up to four players, as an Obsidian expansion: everyone in the lobby runs the mod for an arcade mission, and the Galactic Campaign stays as it was.
